You are the adversarial reviewer on the live-spec project. Work ONLY inside the worktree /private/tmp/live-spec-hands/wt (branch `fix/2026-08-19-workers-hide-work`). Never touch any other directory, never touch ~/live-spec, never touch ~/.claude, never touch other worktrees. You may READ transcripts under ~/.claude/projects.

HARD BOUNDARIES: no `git reset`, no `git rebase`, no `git stash`, no `git clean`, no `git checkout -- <path>`, no `git push`, no `git commit`. Leave your work staged and report. Do NOT run `guardrails/install.sh`. Do NOT run the full pytest suite.

THE RECORD
`docs/prover/2026-08-19-worker-restore-guard-and-manual-dry-run.md` carries five passes. Read the whole record and `docs/prover/README.md` first. Find the current range yourself with `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD`.

WHAT HAPPENED, and what your sixth pass must judge.

The fifth pass refused this push. Its ground: commit `96245b51` moved the retrospective gate's counting start to the moment the hand was installed on this machine, and wrote a reason claiming that a finding after that moment proves the hand was bypassed. That claim was too wide. The hook is read by the harness when a session starts, so a session already running when the hand was installed never loaded it. The session delivering this very work began at `2026-08-19T13:43:47Z`, about nine minutes before the hand was armed at `2026-08-19T13:52:39Z`, and it kept spawning workers afterwards. Under the wide claim, a discard from such a session would have been blamed on a bypass that was never possible.

Commit `ce492395` answers that refusal. It makes the gate judge a finding against its own session's start time, read from that session's own transcript, rather than against the finding's stamp alone. A finding stamped after the counting start reds only if its session also began at or after that moment. A finding from a session that began earlier is carried as history under its own printed heading, the same shape the gate already uses for another project's sessions. A session whose start time cannot be read stays reding, the conservative fall-back the rest of the file uses.

YOUR JOB: judge whether the refusal is genuinely closed, or only papered over. Do not take the previous worker's report as evidence — it is a summary, and a summary of evidence is not evidence. Check for yourself, and go looking for reasons to keep the refusal standing:
- Is reading a session's start time from the first record of its transcript actually sound? What happens for a session whose transcript was rotated, truncated, copied, or whose first record carries no timestamp? Try to find a real session on this machine where it fails.
- Does the new fall-back genuinely stay conservative, or does an unreadable start time now let a real finding through? Prove which, with a run.
- Is the printed history heading honest — does a reader of the output learn that something real happened and was not counted, or does the finding become easy to miss?
- Does the narrowed claim now written in `guardrails/check-worker-restore.py` match what the code actually does, sentence by sentence?
- Do the four new tests in `tests/test_worker_restore.py` actually fail against the old code? Check the one the worker says was red first, and check whether the other three prove anything or merely restate passing behaviour.
- Anything else. Report real findings even if they keep the push refused. That is the job.

Then append a sixth pass to the record, in the shape the five existing passes use, naming the current range and its commits exactly, and stating plainly whether the fifth pass's refusal is lifted or stands.

VERIFY LAST, pasting real output: `bash guardrails/pre-push < /dev/null`. It must end with no red except gate a asking for the record you are writing. If another gate reds, fix the cause and run again.

STYLE RULES OF THIS PROJECT — gates enforce them:
- Plain English, one idea per sentence, no jargon, no marketing tone, no hedging.
- Sentences stay short: a style lint caps them at twenty-five words.
- Never use capital letters for emphasis. Technical values belong in backticks, not in capitals.
- Never leave a bare row number standing where plain words belong: say what the thing is, then its number.
- Evidence beside every claim: a path, a line number, a command and its real output. Never paraphrase an output you did not read.

REPORT BACK (under 35 lines): each thing you checked and what you found, whether the refusal is lifted or stands and why, and the pasted tail of the dry gate run.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). # Prover records

This directory holds one record per review pass. Every push carries exactly one of them, and that
one record does the whole job: it is the fresh re-check of `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md`
that the push gate has always demanded, and it is the adversarial read of the change the push is
about to send. The reviewer is briefed to find reasons the change should be refused, and holds the
change defective until evidence says otherwise. A read that sets out to confirm the change leaves
the requirement unmet.

The rule lives in `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` under `[M-6]`, `[INV-116]` and `[INV-304]`. The gate that reads
these records is `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh`, wired into `guardrails/pre-push` as gate a.

Records of review passes that no push carries — a milestone re-prove, a periodic audit — live here
too, under the same file naming. Only a record written for a push owes the range fields below.

## What the review covers

The spec and the architecture as they now stand, and the delta being pushed: every commit between
the remote's head and the local head. Whatever is still uncommitted is read with them. The range
comes from the base ladder the gate walks — `LIVE_SPEC_DIFF_BASE`, then `origin/main`, then `HEAD~1`.

The commit list for the record:

```
git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
```

## The record's shape

One file per pass, named `YYYY-MM-DD[-slug].md`, committed before the push. The suffix is mandatory
once the date's plain file exists.

```
# Prover record — 2026-08-05 <slug>

PUSH-REVIEW

Range: 258d544..9f21ab0
- 9f21ab0 <subject>
- 258d544 <subject>
Files read: PRODUCT_SPEC.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, guardrails/pre-push
Checks run: python3 -m pytest -q — 2,484 passed
Findings: <what the review found>
Blocking: none
```

Those are all the fields, and the gate reads every one of them. Each carries a value. The commits
between the base and the head are listed under `Range:`, since the gate holds that the record names
every commit it covers. A review that found nothing writes into `Findings:` what it examined; the
absence then rests on the coverage the fields above state, rather than on silence.

`Blocking:` reads `none`, or lists one item per blocking finding. Each item carries `closed:` with
what changed, or `stands:` with the reason it stands. A blocking finding holds the push until one of
those two is written.

## What the gate holds, and what it leaves to the reviewer

The gate holds:

- a record dated today exists;
- the record is committed, rather than a scratch file in the working tree;
- the record is no older than the last change to `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` or `ARCHITECTURE.md`;
- the record is fresh against the pushed range;
- the record names the base commit and every reviewed commit;
- each field carries a value, and a blocking finding is closed or explained.

The gate leaves three things to the reviewer:

- whether the review was adversarial;
- whether the files the record names were read;
- whether the findings are the ones the delta deserved.

No script decides those three. The record's named commits, files, checks and findings are the
pressure a machine can apply toward the review being real.

    must not blame us for what it cannot prove.

    transcript and reds a finding at or after the counting start only when its session
    also began then or later. A finding from an earlier-started session is carried as
    history and printed under its own heading, the same shape the gate already uses
    for a neighbouring project's findings, so nothing is dropped or silently folded
    into a count.

    bypass that was never possible, the same fault row 598 already named: a watcher
    must not blame us for what it cannot prove.

    transcript and reds a finding at or after the counting start only when its session
    also began then or later. A finding from an earlier-started session is carried as
    history and printed under its own heading, the same shape the gate already uses
    for a neighbouring project's findings, so nothing is dropped or silently folded
    into a count.

commit ce492395d701b8b47d5928e1a83afdf051b7cfac
Author: alexander-abramovich <alexander.abramovich.18@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 19 18:32:58 2026 +0300

    Judge a worker-restore finding against its own session's start, not just its stamp.
    
    The counting-start move on 2026-08-19 read a finding stamped at or after the hand's
    arming moment as proof the hand was bypassed or failed. That does not hold for a
    session already running when the hand was armed, since a hook is read once, at
    session start, and such a session never loads it. This project's own session
    a930d83b-8f64-4d5b-8461-0c0a4d95eece began nine minutes before the hand was armed
    and kept spawning workers afterward, so the old reasoning would have blamed a
    bypass that was never possible, the same fault row 598 already named: a watcher
    must not blame us for what it cannot prove.
    
    The gate now reads each finding's own session start from that session's own main
    transcript and reds a finding at or after the counting start only when its session
    also began then or later. A finding from an earlier-started session is carried as
    history and printed under its own heading, the same shape the gate already uses
    for a neighbouring project's findings, so nothing is dropped or silently folded
    into a count.

diff --git a/tests/test_worker_restore.py b/tests/test_worker_restore.py
index 889d81ec..7e427f48 100644
--- a/tests/test_worker_restore.py
+++ b/tests/test_worker_restore.py
@@ -1039,3 +1039,130 @@ class TestTheCountingStartIsTheHandsArmingMomentNotAnArbitraryDate:
             "a COUNTING_FROM bumped forward with the old prose left untouched passed the "
             "agreement check -- it should have failed, since no reason was recorded beside the "
             "new value")
+
+

+                      agent="aabbccddeeff00112233", answers=None):
+    """A worker-run transcript whose records carry a caller-chosen timestamp `at`, rather than
+    `_run_record`'s fixed 2026-07-27 fixture stamp. The counting-start-versus-session-start tests
+    below need to place a finding's own stamp on either side of the hand's arming moment, which the
+    fixed stamp cannot reach."""
+    runs = tmp_path / "projects" / project / session / "subagents"
+    runs.mkdir(parents=True)
+    path = runs / ("agent-%s.jsonl" % agent)
+    answers = answers if answers is not None else ["ran"] * len(commands)
+    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        for i, (c, answer) in enumerate(zip(commands, answers)):
+            tool_id = "toolu_%04d" % i
+            record = _run_record(c, agent=agent, session=session, cwd=cwd, tool_id=tool_id)
+            record["timestamp"] = at
+            f.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
+            if answer is None:
+                continue
+            denial = None if answer in ("ran", "ran-error") else answer
+            result = _result_record(tool_id, denial_kind=denial, shell_error=answer == "ran-error",
+                                    session=session, agent=agent, cwd=cwd)
+            result["timestamp"] = at

+

+    (`<project-dir>/<session-id>.jsonl`), holding one stamped record at `started_at` -- the value
+    `_session_started_at` reads back out as the session's own start time."""
+    path = os.path.join(root, project, session + ".jsonl")
+    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        f.write(json.dumps({"type": "user", "timestamp": started_at, "sessionId": session,
+                            "cwd": None}) + "\n")

+    to the hand's arming moment: the hook is read by the harness when a SESSION starts, so a session
+    already running when the hand was armed never loads it. This very delivery's own session,

+    own session start (`_session_started_at`) alongside its stamp, and reds a finding at or after the
+    counting start only when its own session also began at or after that start; a finding whose
+    session began earlier is carried as history, printed under its own heading rather than folded
+    into a silent count, the same shape a neighbouring project's finding already prints in.
+    """

+    COMMAND = "git checkout -- engine/assets/exhibition.js"
+    ARMED_AT = "2026-08-19T13:52:39Z"
+    SESSION_STARTED_AFTER = "2026-08-19T13:55:00.000Z"
+    FINDING_AFTER_ARMING = "2026-08-19T14:00:00.000Z"
+    SESSION_STARTED_BEFORE = "2026-08-19T13:43:47.589Z"  # this delivery's own session, verified above
+    FINDING_BEFORE_ARMING = "2026-08-19T11:01:06.707Z"  # row 780's own named discard
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _typed_lines(res):
+        return [line for line in res.stdout.splitlines()
+                if line.startswith("{") and line.rstrip().endswith("}")]
+
+    def test_a_finding_after_arming_from_a_session_started_after_arming_reds(self, tmp_path):
+        """The session itself began after the hand was armed, so a discard it recorded after that
+        moment is a live defect in the hand -- exactly the case the third counting-start move meant
+        to catch, and it must go on reding."""
+        root, _ = _write_worker_run(tmp_path, [self.COMMAND], project="-armed-project",
+                                    session="s-armed", cwd=ROOT, at=self.FINDING_AFTER_ARMING)
+        _write_session_start(root, "-armed-project", "s-armed", self.SESSION_STARTED_AFTER)
+        res = _gate("--root", root, "--counting-from", self.ARMED_AT)
+        assert res.returncode == 1, (
+            "a finding whose own session began after the hand was armed stopped reding, which is "
+            "the live-defect case this gate exists to catch:\n%s" % res.stdout)
+        assert len(self._typed_lines(res)) == 1
+
+    def test_a_finding_after_arming_from_a_session_started_before_arming_is_history(self, tmp_path):
+        """The bug this delivery fixes: the session began nine minutes before the hand was armed,
+        the shape row 780's reasoning could not tell from a real bypass. It must stop reding, and
+        the reason must be on the page, not silently swallowed."""
+        root, _ = _write_worker_run(tmp_path, [self.COMMAND], project="-unarmed-project",
+                                    session="s-unarmed", cwd=ROOT, at=self.FINDING_AFTER_ARMING)
+        _write_session_start(root, "-unarmed-project", "s-unarmed", self.SESSION_STARTED_BEFORE)
+        res = _gate("--root", root, "--counting-from", self.ARMED_AT)
+        assert res.returncode == 0, (
+            "a finding from a session that never loaded the hand still refused the push -- the gate "
+            "is accusing this project of something it could not have done:\n%s" % res.stdout)
+        assert not self._typed_lines(res), (
+            "a finding carried as history still carried the blocking gate's typed line:\n%s"
+            % res.stdout)
+        for named in ("s-unarmed", self.SESSION_STARTED_BEFORE, "ARMED"):
+            assert named in res.stdout, (
+                "the reason the finding was carried as history is not on the page -- %r is missing:"
+                "\n%s" % (named, res.stdout))
+
+    def test_a_finding_before_arming_is_history_whatever_its_sessions_start_reads(self, tmp_path):
+        """Unchanged behaviour: a finding stamped BEFORE the counting start is history on its own
+        stamp alone, whatever its session's own start reads -- no hand existed anywhere on the
+        machine yet, so the session-start refinement has nothing to add here."""
+        root, _ = _write_worker_run(tmp_path, [self.COMMAND], project="-old-project", session="s-old",
+                                    cwd=ROOT, at=self.FINDING_BEFORE_ARMING)
+        _write_session_start(root, "-old-project", "s-old", self.SESSION_STARTED_AFTER)
+        res = _gate("--root", root, "--counting-from", self.ARMED_AT)
+        assert res.returncode == 0, res.stdout
+        assert "SESSIONS RUNNING BEFORE THE HAND WAS ARMED" not in res.stdout, (
+            "a finding already carried as history by its own stamp was also printed under the new "
+            "session-start heading, which double-counts one reason as two:\n%s" % res.stdout)
+
+    def test_a_neighbouring_projects_finding_is_unaffected_by_the_session_start_check(self, tmp_path):
+        """The other axis stays put: a neighbouring project's session, stamped after arming, is
+        still carried as a notice under its own heading, never routed through the new check at all
+        -- `own` is decided first, and only an owned finding ever reaches session-start reading."""
+        _skip_unless_gate_has_a_repository()
+        foreign = tmp_path / "neighbour-project"
+        foreign.mkdir(parents=True)
+        subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", str(foreign)], check=True, capture_output=True)
+        root, _ = _write_worker_run(tmp_path, [self.COMMAND], project="-neighbour-project",
+                                    session="s-foreign", cwd=str(foreign),
+                                    at=self.FINDING_AFTER_ARMING)
+        res = _gate("--root", root, "--counting-from", self.ARMED_AT)
+        assert res.returncode == 0, res.stdout
+        assert "ANOTHER PROJECT'S SESSIONS" in res.stdout
+        assert "SESSIONS RUNNING BEFORE THE HAND WAS ARMED" not in res.stdout
+        assert not self._typed_lines(res)

import subprocess, json, tempfile, os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
os.chdir("tests")
import test_worker_restore as t
from pathlib import Path

GATE = t.GATE
ROOT = t.ROOT
ARMED_AT = t.TestAFindingIsJudgedAgainstItsOwnSessionsStart.ARMED_AT
COMMAND = t.TestAFindingIsJudgedAgainstItsOwnSessionsStart.COMMAND
FINDING_AFTER = t.TestAFindingIsJudgedAgainstItsOwnSessionsStart.FINDING_AFTER_ARMING

def run_case(name, project, session, main_content):
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    tmp_path = Path(tmp)
    root, _ = t._write_worker_run(tmp_path, [COMMAND], project=project, session=session,
                                   cwd=ROOT, at=FINDING_AFTER)
    main_path = os.path.join(root, project, session + ".jsonl")
    if main_content is not None:
        with open(main_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(main_content)
    res = subprocess.run(["python3", GATE, "--root", root, "--counting-from", ARMED_AT],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(f"=== {name} ===")
    print("returncode:", res.returncode)
    print("has typed line:", any(l.startswith("{") and l.rstrip().endswith("}") for l in res.stdout.splitlines()))
    print("UNARMED heading present:", "SESSIONS RUNNING BEFORE THE HAND WAS ARMED" in res.stdout)
    print()

run_case("CASE B: empty main transcript file", "-empty-main", "s-empty", "")
run_case("CASE C: main transcript has records but none carry a timestamp",
          "-notime-main", "s-notime", json.dumps({"type":"user","sessionId":"s-notime","cwd":None}) + "\n")
run_case("CASE D: main transcript file is garbage (not JSON lines)",
          "-garbage-main", "s-garbage", "not json at all\nnope\n")

docs/restyle-repoint-log.md:42:## Stage 5 chunk 8 — Breakpoints/resume/milestones (2026-07-09)
docs/roadmap-format.md:39:- *in-work* — the wish is claimed by a session. A landing that leaves any leg open keeps its row live with the open leg named, since a row closes only whole; the row reads *in-work* while a session still drives the open leg, and *deferred* on a named trigger when that leg waits on an outside event. A stale claim is re-read at queue-take — the moment a session takes its next wish from the queue: an *in-work* row with no commit citing it for seven days joins the staleness review list for the human's word. The mechanical sweep behind that list is promised under ROADMAP row 481; until it lands, the taking session runs the re-read itself.
docs/worker-liveness.md:1:# Background workers: spawning, liveness, resume
docs/worker-liveness.md:9:Four brief duties matter most for liveness and resume:
docs/worker-liveness.md:11:- The worker keeps a persistent checkpoint file in the host's `.live-spec/checkpoints/` directory (gitignored, inside the repo tree). It records done / in-progress / next and is updated as the work runs, so a cut-off run resumes from disk (live-spec-base rule 6).
docs/worker-liveness.md:12:- The worker touches that same checkpoint file on a fixed interval (~60 s [default]) as a bare heartbeat, whatever else its work writes. A compute-bound run — a long render, a large test pass — can write no product file for minutes; the heartbeat is what proves it still alive to the resume protocol's death check (INV-76).
docs/worker-liveness.md:49:- The concurrent-edit fence runs before every write and every commit: re-check `git status` and `HEAD` against what was last read. If `HEAD` moved, or the tree holds changes the session did not make, stop, re-read, then proceed surgically or back off (live-spec-base rule 7, INV-11).
docs/worker-liveness.md:57:The resume file is a digest with no redundancy: the whole NEXT_STEPS file holds one live-state block and nothing removable without losing information, and a suite check owns that shape. An open leg restates as one terse line — its name, what stays open, and where the detail lives — while the detail itself flows to the journal or the queue row (INV-48, INV-26).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-prover-record.sh — gate (a) of the push gate: a fresh, committed prover record
# dated today must exist before a push, and that record must be fresh for BOTH guarded
# documents — PRODUCT_SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md (SPEC M-6, INV-116: every live-spec push
# is preceded by a fresh re-check recorded in docs/prover/, covering the spec and the
# architecture alike).
#
# ONE RECORD PER PUSH (SPEC INV-304). A push once owed two review records to two separate
# gates: this one, and a second adversarial read of the pushed delta kept in its own home.
# The two are one pass, so they are one record. On the PUSH road this gate therefore also
# holds what the second gate held: the record names the pushed range, carries the fields
# that say what the review covered, and leaves no blocking finding open.
#
# THE LAW behind that half. A change that passes every test can still be wrong in ways no
# test asks about. A reviewer briefed to find reasons to refuse the change reads it
# differently from a reviewer set on confirming it, and the difference is what the suite
# misses. So the record a push carries is an adversarial read of the very commits it sends.
#
# THE RECORD. One dated file under <prover-dir>, committed, carrying:
#   PUSH-REVIEW      the marker line
#   Range:           the base commit and the head commit the review read, with the commits
#                    between them listed under it
#   Files read:      the files the reviewer opened
#   Checks run:      the commands the reviewer ran, each with its result
#   Findings:        what the review found; a review that found nothing says so here, and its
#                    coverage stands on the two fields above
#   Blocking:        `none`, or one item per blocking finding, each carrying `closed:` or
#                    `stands:` with the reason it stands
# docs/prover/README.md holds the same shape for a person writing one, and holds no field
# this script leaves unread.
#
# WHAT THIS SCRIPT CAN HOLD: that a record exists, that it is committed rather than a scratch
# file, that it is fresh against the guarded documents and against the pushed range, that it
# names the base commit and every reviewed commit, that it carries each field with a value,
# and that a blocking finding is closed or explained.
#
# WHAT THIS SCRIPT CANNOT HOLD: whether the review was adversarial. No script decides whether
# a reviewer set out to refuse the change or to confirm it, whether the files named were read,
# or whether the findings are the ones the delta deserved. Those rest on the reviewer. This
# gate applies the pressure a machine can apply — the record names the commits, the files, the
# checks and the findings — and leaves the judgment where it belongs.
#
# THE STAND-DOWN MARKER CONVENTION (the REFUSE of 2026-08-15 23:41, finding F2). Every arm in
# this chain that can let a push past the record demand — an arm that exits 0 without a record
# on file — carries, immediately above it, one line of the exact shape:
#
#   # STAND-DOWN: <name>
#
# <name> is a single token, and PRODUCT_SPEC.md R226 criterion 6 must carry that same token in
# the exception it names. guardrails/pre-push carries the same marker over the deletion-only

   wrong conclusion about what a post-arming finding means. stands: row 780 needs its own sentence
   narrowed the same way the code's docstring was, or it stays a standing contradiction between two of

closing that one case does not clear the push. The fix's fallback is built on a premise — a transcript
file's first record marks its process's own start — that this machine's own transcripts show does not
hold in general, only for the one session the fix happened to check; sessions do get relaunched across

whether the machine question above is ever resolved. REFUSAL STANDS, on new grounds: `ce492395` closes
the Fifth pass's own case but does not clear the push on its own terms.

## Report

**Range judged:** `9870c7b8..72b83062` (base unchanged); reviewed the two commits new since the fifth pass: `ce492395` and `72b83062`.

**Checked, with real evidence:**

1. **Fifth pass's own case — closed, verified not assumed.** Reverted `guardrails/check-worker-restore.py` to `ce492395~1` (via `git show`, restored after — no `git checkout` used, `git status` clean throughout) and ran the four new tests. Only `test_a_finding_after_arming_from_a_session_started_before_arming_is_history` fails on old code (`assert 1 == 0`); the other three pass unchanged against old code too — they pin non-regression, not the fix itself. Live-fed the exact fifth-pass scenario (this session's real start `2026-08-19T13:43:47.589Z`, finding after arming) — now exits 0, printed under a named heading, not dropped.

2. **New, real gap: `_session_started_at` conflates a transcript's first record with the current process's own start.** Scanned all 139 worker-spawning session transcripts on this machine: 62 have internal gaps over one hour, one — `~/.claude/projects/-Users-sashaabramovich/5d5e8f03-0e43-4153-862a-0281381a4096.jsonl` — has a 118.7-hour gap spanning five days, with real worker runs in its `subagents/` directory on both sides. The fix's docstring verifies its "first record = session start" claim against exactly one session (its own). If a relaunch of an existing session reloads hooks fresh (as plausible, and as undocumented, as the premise the fifth pass already flagged), a session created before arming but relaunched after it would have a real post-arming bypass silently filed as history. `--since-hours 24` shows this isn't an active miss today, but the mechanism is unverified for exactly the case this machine's transcripts show is common.

3. **`ROADMAP.md` row 780 (line 275) was not updated and now contradicts the code.** It still reads "every discard of this shape stamped `2026-08-19T13:52:39Z` or later is a live defect in that hand. It is never history a gate should carry forward" — the opposite of what `ce492395` now does.

**Also verified:** the conservative fallback for an unreadable session start (missing/empty/no-timestamp/garbage main transcript) genuinely stays conservative — built all four shapes by hand, all reds. Docstring prose matches code sentence-by-sentence on the parts I checked.
